column2: Narayana is the highest truth; the true order is of Narayana's nature; the highest dharma is Narayana, hard to find for return.
The dharma marked by action is of Narayana's nature; smell, the best quality of earth, is remembered as of Narayana's nature.
And the quality of waters, O king, taste, is of Narayana's nature; form, the quality of luminaries, is remembered as of Narayana's nature.
Touch, the quality of wind, is remembered as of Narayana's nature; sound, born of space, is also of Narayana's nature.
Then mind too is an element, marked by the qualities of the unmanifest; Time is supremely Narayana, and what is the course of the luminaries.
Fame, Shri, Lakshmi and the goddesses have Narayana as their highest; Sankhya has Narayana as highest; yoga is of Narayana's nature.
For those whose cause is the Person, and those whose cause is Pradhana, nature, action, or fate,
called the five causes, Hari is the end everywhere, for those who seek the truth by reasons facing every way.
The one truth is the yogi Hari Narayana, the lord, of the worlds with Brahma and of the great-souled sages,
of the Sankhyas, yogis, ascetics and knowers of the self; Keshava knows their wish, but they do not know his.
Whoever in all worlds perform rites for gods and ancestors, give gifts, and practise great austerity,
Vishnu is the refuge of all, standing in lordly rule, the dwelling made for all beings, and is called Vasudeva.
This is the eternal supreme great sage, of great glory, with qualities and called without qualities, and quickly joins with qualities, as Time joins with the seasons in their season.
The great souls do not find his course, nor does anyone here see his non-course; the great sages, self-controlled, of the nature of knowledge, always see the Person who exceeds the qualities.
[Janamejaya said:] Those in the world who have burnt their fuel, free of merit and sin: for them you have indicated the goal that has come down by tradition.
In the fourth state they go to the Supreme Person; but the single-minded go to the highest state.
Surely this single-minded dharma is best and dear to Narayana, since they go to the imperishable Hari without going the three paths.
The brahmins who rightly stand in the Vedas with the Upanishads, who recite by rule, and those who follow the dharma of ascetics,
I know the goal of single-minded men to be better than theirs. By what god or sage was this dharma told?
What is the conduct of the single-minded, and when was it produced, lord? Cut this doubt of mine; my curiosity is great.
[Vaishampayana said:] When the armies stood ready in the battle of the Kurus and Pandavas, and Arjuna was dispirited, it was sung by the blessed one himself.
The coming and the going were told to you by me before; this dharma is deep, hard to know for the unpractised.
This vow, recited in the reading of the Rig Veda, is hard to practise; this eternal dharma was also gained from Suparna.
It was made known by Vayu, best of the two-footed, the life of the world; it was gained from Vayu by sages who eat the remnants.
From them the great ocean gained this excellent dharma; then he vanished again, absorbed in Narayana.
Listen to the recounting, tiger among men, of when there was again a creation, born of the ear, of the great Brahma.
Wishing to create the world, the god Hari Narayana himself thought of the Person, the maker of the world's creation.
Then, as he thought, from his ears a Person issued, Brahma the maker of creation, and the lord of the world spoke to him:

Create all creatures, son, from the mouth and from the feet; I shall ordain your good, strength and splendour, of good vows.
mahabharata:12:336.27	And take from me the dharma named Satvata; by that establish the whole Krita age by rule.
Then Brahma bowed to the god of Hari's wisdom and received the best dharma with its secret and compendium, together with the Aranyaka, issued from Narayana's mouth.
Having taught the dharma to Brahma of boundless splendour, the Krita-age dharma called action without desire, he went beyond darkness to where the unmanifest stands.
Then the boon-giving god, Brahma, grandfather of the world, created all worlds, moving and unmoving.
Then the lovely Krita age began, at the beginning; and the Satvata dharma stood pervading the worlds.
By that primal dharma Brahma, the creator of the worlds, worshipped the lord of gods Hari Narayana.
For the establishment of dharma, he then taught it to Manu Svarochisha, wishing the good of the worlds.
Then Svarochisha's son Shankhapada, king, was himself taught unperturbed by the all-pervading lord of the world.
Then Shankhapada taught his own son, Sudharman, guardian of the quarter, Bharata; then he vanished again, and the Treta age came.
In Brahma's nose-born birth long ago, the god Hari Narayana, the lotus-eyed lord, himself brought up this dharma, best of kings, as Brahma watched.
The blessed Sanatkumara then studied it, king; and from Sanatkumara the Prajapati Virana studied this dharma at the start of the Krita age, tiger of the Kurus.
And Virana, having studied it, gave it to Manu Raucya; Raucya to his pure son of good vows and good wisdom.
Then he gave it to the righteous guardian of the quarter named Kukshi; then it vanished again, issued from Narayana's mouth.
In the egg-born birth, again, this dharma arose again from Narayana's mouth for Brahma, whose womb is Hari.
Taken by Brahma, O king, and duly applied, it was taught to the sages named Barhishads, king.
From the Barhishads it passed to the twice-born Jyeshtha, master of the end of the Sama Veda, famous by name, Hari fixed on the Jyeshtha Sama vow.
From Jyeshtha it passed to King Avikampana, and then, O king, this dharma of the lord Hari vanished.
In this seventh birth of Brahma, the lotus-born, O king, this dharma was told there by Narayana himself.
To the pure grandfather, at the start of the age, the bearer of the world, and the grandfather long ago gave this dharma to Daksha.
Then Daksha gave it to the eldest of his daughter's sons, best of kings, to Aditya Savitri's eldest, and Vivasvan took it.
At the start of the Treta age Vivasvan again gave it to Manu, and Manu gave it to his son Ikshvaku for the good of the world.
Told by Ikshvaku, it stays pervading the worlds, and at the end of the age, O king, it will go again to Narayana.
The dharma of those with vows, which I told you before, best of kings, was ordained in the Hari Gita in a concise rule.
This dharma with its secret and compendium was received by Narada directly from the lord of the world Narayana, O king.
Thus this great dharma, primal and eternal, O king, hard to know and hard to practise, is always borne by the Satvatas.
By this knowledge of dharma, with well-applied action joined with non-violence and dharma, Hari the lord is pleased.
The division is sometimes of one arrangement, sometimes called twofold, and counted threefold, and seen fourfold.
Hari alone is the knower of the field, free of mine-ness and parts, and the soul in all beings, beyond the qualities of the five elements.
And mind is known, O king, as the mover of the five senses; he is the treasure of the world, the wise, the maker of creation.
He is the non-doer and the doer, the effect and the cause; as he wishes, king, so the imperishable Person plays.
This single-minded dharma has been told to you, best of kings, by me through my teacher's grace, hard to know for the unpractised; single-minded men are rare, O king, and many.
If the world were filled with the single-minded, non-violent, knowers of the self, delighting in the good of all beings, then the Krita age would come, free of wishes and action.
Thus the blessed Vyasa, my teacher, O lord of men, best of the twice-born, knower of dharma, told it to the king of dharma.
In the presence of the sages, O king, as Krishna and Bhishma listened, and Narada of great austerity had earlier told it to him.
The supreme god, Brahman, white, moon-bright, unfallen, where the single-minded go, with Narayana as their supreme refuge.
[Janamejaya said:] If this dharma of many kinds is practised by the awakened, why do other brahmins, standing in various vows, not practise it?
[Vaishampayana said:] Three natures, O king, are made in the bonds of bodies: sattvic, rajasic and tamasic, Bharata.
In the bonds of bodies, lifter of the Kuru line, the best person is the sattvic, tiger among men, who is resolved on liberation.
Here too he knows the Person present in Brahman; liberation is supremely Narayana, so the sattvic is remembered.
He attains what he wishes, contemplating the Supreme Person, with single-minded devotion constantly, intent on Narayana.
For whatever wise ascetics long for liberation, whose thirst is cut, Hari carries their winning and keeping.
The person whom, as he is born, Madhusudana sees is to be known as sattvic and is certain of liberation.
Dharma practised single-mindedly is equal to Sankhya and yoga; in liberation of Narayana's nature, they go to the highest goal.
A man seen by Narayana becomes awakened; thus, by the will of the self, O king, the awakened is not born.
Rajasic and tamasic natures are remembered as mixed; the person of that nature, lord of men, when being born, joined with marks of action, Hari himself does not regard.
Brahma, grandfather of the world, sees him as he is born, a man overwhelmed by rajas and tamas.
Gods and sages standing in sattva, best of kings, by choice, lacking subtle sattva, are then remembered as modified.
[Janamejaya said:] How would the modified person go to the Supreme Person?
[Vaishampayana said:] Joined with very subtle sattva, joined with the three letters, the person, inactive, goes to the twenty-fifth Person.
Thus Sankhya and yoga, the Veda and Aranyaka are one; these are mutual limbs, and the Pancharatra is told. This is the dharma of the single-minded, of Narayana's highest nature.
As floods of water issued from the ocean enter it again, O king, so these great floods of knowledge enter Narayana again.
This Satvata dharma has been told to you, kinsman of the Yadavas; practise it duly if you can, Bharata.
Thus the greatly fortunate Narada told my teacher the imperishable single-minded goal of the white ascetics.
Vyasa told it with affection to the wise son of Dharma; this same is what has been told to you by me, issued from my teacher.
Thus this dharma is hard to practise, best of kings; as you, so others, bewildered, do not follow it.
Krishna alone is the cherisher and the bewilderer of the worlds, O lord of men, the destroyer, and the cause.
[Janamejaya said:] Are these of one end or of separate ends, sage? Tell me, as I ask, and the course of action in order.

[Vaishampayana said:] I bow to him who removes the darkest ignorance, the great seer, born of Parashara and Gandhavati, the knowing and self-possessed son born in the middle of an island, very noble in mind.
I bow to Dvaipayana, whom they call the sixth from the grandfather, a great sage joined with the glory of the sages, born of a part of Narayana, an only son, a great treasury of the Veda.
Narayana, of great glory, the Brahman, a great treasury, of generous splendour, the unborn ancient one, created him at the beginning for a son, Vyasa the great soul.
[Janamejaya said:] You yourself told me before his birth, best of the twice-born: Vasishtha's son Shakti, and Shakti's son Parashara.
The sage Krishna Dvaipayana is Parashara's heir; yet you again call him Narayana's son.
What earlier birth had Vyasa of boundless splendour? Tell it, wise one, the birth that arose from Narayana.
[Vaishampayana said:] To my teacher, who wished to know the meaning of the Vedas, righteous, a store of austerity, firm in knowledge, seated at the foot of the Himalaya,
Knowing the truth, having first told the meaning of the Vedas and of the Bharata, he began to tell this birth from Narayana.
Hear this best of accounts, a sages' tale, excellent, arisen at the beginning of time, got by me through austerity, brahmins.
When the seventh creation of creatures came, at the lotus-born, Narayana, the great yogi, free of good and bad,
created from his navel a son, Brahma of boundless radiance; then he appeared and he spoke to him:
You were born from my navel, lord, maker of creation; create creatures of many kinds, Brahmana, with the wise.
Thus told by me, Brahma, turned away, his mind agitated with worry, bowed to the boon-giving god Hari the lord and said:
What strength have I, lord of gods, to create creatures? Homage to you. I am without wisdom, god; ordain what follows.
Thus told by him, the blessed one, becoming hidden, the lord of gods, best of the wise, thought of understanding.
Then understanding, embodied, came to Hari the lord, and the Unyoked himself joined her to him by yoga.
To that understanding standing in lordly yoga, powerful and good, the god, the imperishable lord, said:
Enter Brahma, for the accomplishment of creating the worlds. Then, commanded by the lord, understanding quickly entered him.
Then Hari saw him joined with understanding and again said to him: "Create these various creatures."
Having said so, the blessed one vanished right there, and by him again was reached the place called the gods' own.
And reaching that same nature, he became one with it; then, it is said, another thought arose in him:

All these creatures have been created by Brahma Parameshthi, thronged with Daityas, Danavas, gandharvas and hosts of rakshasas; this earth, born, is burdened and suffering.
mahabharata:12:337.30	Many mighty Daityas, Danavas and Rakshasas will be on the earth; joined with austerity, they will gain excellent boons.
mahabharata:12:337.31	Surely, made proud by the boons, they will harass the hosts of gods and the ascetic sages. Here it is just for me to do the lifting of the burden.
mahabharata:12:337.32	Then, by being born in various forms on the earth in order, by restraining the wicked and favouring the good,
mahabharata:12:337.33	I shall support this suffering, true earth; for she is supported by me as the serpent in the nether world.
mahabharata:12:337.34	Supported by me, she supports the world with its moving and unmoving; therefore I shall save the earth, going into birth.
Thus having thought, the blessed Madhusudana created many forms for the sake of manifestation:
boar, man-lion, dwarf and man. "By these the wicked enemies of the gods are to be slain by me."
Then the creator of the world again, resounding with the word "Bho!", uttered Sarasvati, and the Sarasvata was born there.
His son, named Apantaratamas, born of speech, of the lord, knew past, present and future, truthful, firm in vows.
The imperishable first of the gods said to him as he bowed his head: "You must compile the Veda; therefore, sage, do my word as ordered."
By him the Vedas were then divided in the Svayambhuva interval of Manu; then the blessed Hari was pleased with his work, with austerity well practised, with restraint and observance.
[The Blessed One said:] "In the intervals of Manus, son, you will thus be a promoter of the worlds, unshaken, Brahmana, and always unassailable.
And again when Tishya comes, there will be great-souled Bharata kings called Kurus, famed on earth.
Among those born of you there will be a breach of the family, for their mutual destruction, because of you, best of the twice-born.
There too you, joined with austerity, will divide the Vedas in many ways, and when the dark age comes you will be dark-coloured.
You will be the maker of various dharmas and the creator of knowledge; joined with austerity, you will not be freed from attachment.
Your son, free of attachment, will be the Supreme Self by Maheshvara's grace; this word is not otherwise.
He whom they call the mind-born son of the grandfather, joined with excellent understanding, Vasishtha, best, a treasury of austerity, who shines surpassing even the sun,

in his line comes the great sage of great power named Parashara; he is your father, treasury of the Veda, best, of great austerity, dwelling of austerity; with a maiden's womb of the ancestors, you will be born as the son of that sage.
All doubts of the meaning of past, present and future will be cut for you; and the revolutions of thousand ages that have passed before,
all those told by me you will see, joined with austerity, and you will again see revolutions of many thousand ages.
You will see me in the world, without beginning or end, wheel in hand, sage, by meditation on me; this word is not otherwise.
Shanaishchara, son of the Sun, will be the great Manu, and in that Manu's interval you yourself will be the first of the group of seven sages, child, by my grace, without doubt."
[Vyasa said:] Having thus spoken to the sage Apantaratamas, Sarasvata, the lord then said, "Accomplish it."
By the grace of that god of Hari's wisdom I am Apantaratamas, and by Hari's command was born again and famed as the delight of Vasishtha's line.
This earlier birth of mine has been told, and likewise the birth from a part of Narayana by Narayana's grace.
For very great and most severe austerity was practised by me long ago, best of the wise, with supreme concentration.
All this you asked me, children, past birth and future, has been told to you out of affection for devotees.
[Vaishampayana said:] This was told to you earlier, king, the birth of our teacher Vyasa of untroubled mind; as you asked, hear it again.
Sankhya, yoga, Pancharatra, the Vedas and Pashupata: know these as various views of knowledge, royal sage.
The speaker of Sankhya is called the supreme sage Kapila; Hiranyagarbha is the knower of yoga, and no other ancient.
Apantaratamas is called the teacher of the Veda; some here call that sage Prachinagarbha.
Uma's lord, the lord of beings, Shrikantha, Brahma's son, Shiva, unperturbed, spoke this Pashupata knowledge.
The knower of the whole Pancharatra is the blessed one himself, and he is seen in all these knowledges, best of kings.
According to tradition and knowledge the end is the lord Narayana, but those who have become tamas do not know him so, O lord of men.
The wise call him the maker of the scripture, and say there is none other than the sage Narayana as the end.
Hari ever dwells in all who are free of doubt; Madhava does not dwell in the doubting by strength of arguments.
Those who know the Pancharatra and follow the order, O king, having attained single-minded devotion, enter Hari.
Sankhya and yoga are two eternal ones, and all the Vedas entire, O king; by all the sages together, Narayana is declared the universe, the ancient.
Whatever action, good or bad, is set going and proceeds in all worlds, let one know it arises from that sage, in heaven, sky, earth and the waters.
[Vaishampayana said:] Many are the persons in the world; those who reflect on Sankhya and yoga do not accept the Person as one, lifter of the Kuru line.
As one womb is said of many persons, so I shall explain that Person as the universe, above the qualities.
Having bowed to the teacher Vyasa of boundless splendour, joined with austerity, self-controlled, worthy of salutation, the supreme sage,
this Purusha Sukta, O king, is in all the Vedas, known as the true and the real, reflected on by the lion among sages.
By general rule and exception, the scriptures were told by the sages, Kapila and the rest, resorting to reflection on the self, Bharata.
What Vyasa said in brief on the oneness of the Person, that I shall tell you, by the grace of the one of boundless power.
On this too they recount this ancient Itihasa, a conversation of Tryambaka with Brahma, lord of men.
In the middle of the Milk Ocean is a mountain, best of mountains, bright as gold, famed as Vaijayanta, O king.
And the blessed one said to his son who had long been away: "Welcome, mighty-armed; by good fortune you have come near me.
Is it well with you, son, in study and austerity always? For you are always of fierce austerity; so I ask you again."
[Rudra said:] "By your grace, blessed one, it is well with my study and austerity, and imperishably well with all the world.
I saw the blessed one long ago in the abode of Vairaja; then I have come to this mountain served by your feet.
And I have curiosity about your going into solitude, grandfather; this cause cannot be small.
What is that best abode, free of hunger and thirst, inhabited by gods and asuras and by sages of boundless splendour,
constantly served by gandharvas and apsarases? Leaving this best of mountains, you have come here alone."
[Brahma said:] "The best of mountains Vaijayanta is constantly served by me; here with one-pointed mind the Person, Virat, is contemplated."
[Rudra said:] "Many persons, Brahmana, were created by you, the self-existent, and others are being created, Brahmana; and he is one Person, Virat.
Who is that Supreme Person contemplated by you, Brahmana? Tell me this doubt; my curiosity is great."
[Brahma said:] "Many persons, son, are those you have named; so what is past, and is to be seen, not this; but I shall tell the support of the one Person for you.
As one womb is said of many persons, so that Person, the universe, supreme, greatest, without qualities: becoming without qualities, they enter the eternal one without qualities."

He cannot be seen by you or me or others, good one; with qualities, without qualities, universal, he is remembered as seen by knowledge.
mahabharata:12:339.3	Bodiless, he dwells in all bodies; though dwelling in bodies, he is not stained by deeds.
mahabharata:12:339.4	The inner self of me and of you and of the others called embodied, he is the witness of all, to be grasped by none anywhere.
mahabharata:12:339.5	With the universe for head, arms, feet, eyes and nose, he moves alone in the fields, roaming freely at will.
mahabharata:12:339.6	Fields are bodies, and good and bad are seeds; he knows them, the yoga-self, and therefore is called the knower of the field.
mahabharata:12:339.7	His coming and going are not to be known by any being, by Sankhya rule or by yoga in order.
mahabharata:12:339.8	I think of his course, and do not know the highest course; but as knowledge is, I shall tell of that eternal Person.
mahabharata:12:339.9	His oneness and greatness: he is remembered as the one Person; he alone, the eternal, bears the name Great Person.
mahabharata:12:339.10	One fire is kindled in many ways; one sun is the source of heat; one wind blows in many ways in the world; one great ocean is the source of waters; and one Person, without qualities, of universal form, they enter that Person without qualities.

mahabharata:12:339.12	Knowing him too as inconceivable, subtle by nature, fourfold, the ascetic who lives with effort goes to the lord Person.
mahabharata:12:339.13	Some wise men so wish the Supreme Self, others, reflecting on the self, wish the self as one.
mahabharata:12:339.14	There the Supreme Self is remembered as always without qualities; he is to be known as Narayana, the self of all, the Person; he is not stained by fruits, like a lotus leaf by water.
mahabharata:12:339.15	But the other, the self of action, is joined with the bonds of liberation, and is joined with the heap of seventeen. Thus the Person has been told to you in many ways in order.
mahabharata:12:339.16	That which is the whole abode of the system of the world, the highest knowable, the awakener with the awakened one, the thinker, the thinkable, the taster, the tasteable, the smeller, the smellable, the toucher, the touchable,
mahabharata:12:339.17	the seer, the seeable, the hearer, the hearable, the knower, the knowable, with qualities and without qualities, what is called the equilibrium of qualities, Pradhana, eternal, everlasting and imperishable,
mahabharata:12:339.18	what produces the first treasure of the creator, that, brahmins, they call Aniruddha. What in the world is good Vedic action joined with wishes, that is to be enjoyed by him.
mahabharata:12:339.19	All the gods and the good, self-controlled sages worship him first with sacrifices as the share of sacrifice. I, Brahma, the first lord of creatures, and you, born of me, and from me the moving and unmoving world, and all the Vedas with their secrets, son.
Fourfold divided the Person plays as he wishes; thus the blessed one himself was awakened by knowledge.
This has been told to you, son, as you asked; it has been described truly in Sankhya knowledge and in yoga.
And you, tiger among men, ought to hear from me a story told to Shakra long ago by the divine sage Narada.
The divine sage Narada, O king, perfected, honoured in the three worlds, goes through the worlds in order, like the unobstructed wind.
Once that great archer went to the abode of the king of the gods, was honoured by Mahendra, and sat close.
As he sat at leisure the lord of Shachi asked him: "Brahmarishi, sinless one, have you seen any wonder?
As you, brahmana sage, roam the three worlds with their moving and unmoving, always curious, perfected, like a witness,
there is nothing unknown to you in the world, divine sage; tell me what you have heard, felt or seen."

Having fulfilled the householder's dharma, lord of brahmanas, and gone to the sons' stage, I would practise the highest dharma; what, Brahmana, would be the way?
mahabharata:12:342.3	I wish to be one with the self in the self, alone and abiding in the self; I do not wish to be bound by common qualities.
mahabharata:12:342.4	As long as my age relying on the fruit of sons has not passed, so long I wish to take provisions for the other world.
mahabharata:12:342.5	For one who wishes the farther shore in this line of the world, this thought has arisen in me: where is the raft made of dharma?
mahabharata:12:342.6	Hearing of the world being swept along and sattvic things being given up, and seeing the garland of the banner of dharma scattered over creatures,
mahabharata:12:342.7	my mind does not delight at the time of enjoyment, seeing ascetics beseeching the beyond. Therefore, guest, by the strength of your understanding, engage me in the truth of dharma and wealth.
I shall conquer death as a householder: thus, lord, the wise Sudarshana, radiant, made his vow, O lord of men.
I wish to sacrifice with him; my materials are gathered; I am to be sacrificed for by you, good one; accept it and arrange it.
[Vaishampayana said:] Thus told by his elder father, the son of Kunti, Bharata, gently touched all his limbs out of affection.

The hunter Jara, mistaking Keshava, lying absorbed in yoga, for a deer, pierced the sole of his foot with an arrow and hastened to seize him; then the hunter saw a man absorbed in yoga, in yellow garments, with many arms.
Neither Krishna the king's daughter nor any other is fit for hell, Yudhishthira; come, come, best of the Bharatas, see the Ganga that goes through the three worlds.
